content: The safety and efficacy of SEREVENT DISKUS have been established through adequate and well-controlled clinical trials conducted in both adults and adolescents. A significant 28-week placebo-controlled trial in the United States compared salmeterol (SEREVENT Inhalation Aerosol) with placebo, both added to usual asthma therapy. This study revealed an increase in asthma-related deaths among subjects receiving salmeterol. Post-hoc analyses were also conducted in pediatric subjects aged 12 to 18 years, who represented approximately 12% of the participants in each treatment group. The safety and efficacy of SEREVENT DISKUS were evaluated in over 2,500 pediatric subjects aged 4 to 11 years with asthma, including 346 subjects who received SEREVENT DISKUS for one year. Based on the available data, no dosage adjustment of SEREVENT DISKUS is necessary for pediatric patients with asthma or exercise-induced bronchospasm (EIB). In two randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trials lasting 12 weeks, SEREVENT DISKUS 50 mcg was administered to 211 pediatric subjects with asthma, both with and without concurrent inhaled corticosteroids. The efficacy of SEREVENT DISKUS was demonstrated over the 12-week treatment period, as evidenced by improvements in peak expiratory flow (PEF) and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1). SEREVENT DISKUS was effective across demographic subgroups, including gender and age. As with all inhaled sympathomimetic medications, an overdose of SEREVENT DISKUS may result in cardiac arrest and even death. Treatment for overdose involves discontinuation of SEREVENT DISKUS and the administration of appropriate symptomatic therapy. The cautious use of a cardioselective beta-receptor blocker may be considered, although such medications can induce bronchospasm. There is insufficient evidence to determine whether dialysis is beneficial in cases of SEREVENT DISKUS overdose. Cardiac monitoring is recommended in overdose situations. The pharmacologic effects of beta2-adrenergic receptor agonists, including salmeterol, are partially attributed to the stimulation of intracellular adenyl cyclase, an enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cyclic AMP). Increased cyclic AMP levels lead to relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle and inhibition of the release of immediate hypersensitivity mediators, particularly from mast cells. In vitro studies demonstrate that salmeterol is a potent and long-lasting inhibitor of mast cell mediator release, including histamine, leukotrienes, and prostaglandin D2, from human lung tissue. Salmeterol also inhibits histamine-induced plasma protein extravasation and platelet-activating factor-induced eosinophil accumulation in the lungs of guinea pigs when administered via inhalation. In humans, single doses of salmeterol delivered via inhalation aerosol reduce allergen-induced bronchial hyperresponsiveness. The effects of increasing inhaled doses of salmeterol and standard doses of albuterol were studied in both healthy volunteers and asthma patients. Salmeterol doses up to 84 mcg administered via inhalation aerosol caused heart rate increases of 3 to 16 beats per minute, comparable to albuterol dosed at 180 mcg via inhalation aerosol, which caused increases of 4 to 10 beats per minute. Continuous electrocardiographic monitoring of adult and adolescent subjects receiving 50-mcg doses of salmeterol inhalation powder (n = 60) during two 12-hour periods after the first dose and after one month of therapy revealed no clinically significant dysrhythmias. Similarly, pediatric patients receiving 50-mcg doses of salmeterol inhalation powder (n = 67) underwent continuous electrocardiographic monitoring during two 12-hour periods after the first dose and after three months of therapy, with no clinically significant dysrhythmias observed. In 24-week clinical studies involving patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), the incidence of clinically significant abnormalities on pre-dose electrocardiograms (ECGs) at Weeks 12 and 24 in patients receiving salmeterol 50 mcg was not different from those receiving placebo. No effect of salmeterol 50 mcg treatment was observed on pulse rate or systolic and diastolic blood pressure in a subset of COPD patients who underwent 12-hour serial vital sign measurements after the first dose (n = 91) and after 12 weeks of therapy (n = 74). Median changes from baseline in pulse rate and blood pressure were similar between patients receiving salmeterol and those receiving placebo. In two 12-week, repeat-dose clinical trials involving adult and adolescent asthma patients (N = 149), the mean daily need for additional short-acting beta2-agonists among subjects using SEREVENT DISKUS was approximately 1.5 inhalations per day. However, 26% of subjects in these trials used between 8 and 24 inhalations of short-acting beta-agonists per day on one or more occasions.
